state.misconception_label: Ignores negative sign when expanding bracket

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: John is expanding these three brackets: \( (x+5)(x-3)(x+6) \) He finds it helpful to split the first bracket and view the problem as follows: \( x(x-3)(x+6)+5(x-3)(x+6) \) He expands the brackets further. Before he simplifies, what are the terms than contain an \( \boldsymbol{x}^{2} \) ? I got \( \begin{array}{l}+6 x^{2} \\ +3 x^{2} \\ +5 x^{2}\end{array} \) because I forgot that two negatives multiply to a positive.

  2. Topic: Expand double brackets with an extra variable outside. Correct answer (A): \( \triangle=-25 \). Student selected: \( \triangle=+25 \). Underlying misconception: Believes multiplying a positive by a negative gives a positive answer. Intervention focus: surface why the selected answer is wrong and walk through the reasoning that leads to the correct answer.
  3. Topic: Carry out multiplication problems involving one negative integer. Correct answer (B): \( -15 \). Student selected: \( +2 \). Underlying misconception: Adds instead of multiplying when expanding bracket. Intervention focus: surface why the selected answer is wrong and walk through the reasoning that leads to the correct answer.
